questions.question: Which type of brackets is standardly used to define a Tuple collection in Python?
questions.explanation: Spot on! Tuples are constructed using round parentheses (), whereas lists use square brackets [], and dictionaries use curly brackets {}.

questions.question: What is the primary difference between a Python List and a Python Tuple?
options: Tuples can only hold text strings
Lists are changeable (mutable), while Tuples are completely unchangeable (immutable)
Lists use parentheses; tuples use square brackets
There is no difference between them
questions.explanation: Correct! Tuples are immutable, which means once you declare their items, you cannot edit, add, or delete elements from them.

questions.question: How are individual items represented inside a Python Dictionary collection?
options: As ordered items starting from index [0]
As unique key:value pairs associated together
questions.explanation: Excellent! Dictionaries store data in key:value pairs (e.g. 'color':'red'), making it easy to map descriptive values to unique tags.

questions.question: If you try to add a duplicate key to an existing Python dictionary, what will happen?
options: The program will crash with an error
The old value will be overwritten by the new value since duplicate keys are not allowed
The dictionary will delete all its values
It will create a tuple inside the dictionary
questions.explanation: Great! Dictionaries do not allow duplicate keys. Setting an existing key to a new value simply replaces the old value.

questions.question: Simple Coding Task: Given the dictionary car = {'brand': 'Ford', 'year': 2020}. Write a Python statement to access and print the value of the 'brand' key.
questions.explanation: Perfect! You can fetch any value from a dictionary by putting its associated key name inside square brackets next to the dictionary variable.

questions.question: Simple Coding Task: Create a tuple named 'fruits' containing three strings: 'apple', 'banana', 'cherry', and print the fruits tuple.
questions.explanation: Outstanding! Creating collections using round brackets declares immutable tuples, securing your data from accidental changes.
